heading: INT. ABANDONED SALT MINE - CURLING SHEET - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ABANDONED SALT MINE - CURLING SHEET - NIGHT
A white rock hall lit by work lamps strung from roof bolts.
Brine has been frozen into a ribbon of ice sixty feet long.
The air tastes of metal.
ODALYS FERREIRA, forties, crouches at the hack with her broom held like a rifle.
She does not look at the score chalked on the wall.
Nobody does.
BRUNO KATZ, her skip, broad as a doorway, stands in the far house and taps the ice with his broom.
He taps it again.
He taps it again.
TAMSIN OYELARAN, nineteen, and KOFI, thirties, a union jacket zipped to the chin, crouch on either side of the lane, brooms raised, breath smoking.
Hold.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Odalys slides.
The stone leaves her hand and the whole hall leans after it.
Tamsin and Kofi run beside it, sweeping in a frantic double rhythm, their brooms drumming the ice, each trying to outpace the other.
Hard. Hard.
units.name: BRUNO

units.text: At the rail, WREN, a girl of ten in a hard hat three sizes too big, grips the cold pipe with both hands.
ISHAAN, her father, sixty, puts his palm on the back of her helmet and neither of them blinks.
The stone slows.
Tamsin and Kofi both stop sweeping at the same instant and stand there, brooms hovering, like men who have seen a wire pulled tight.
The stone creeps, touches the button, and settles against the opposing rock with a small clean click.
Nobody cheers.
Bruno lowers his broom and sets it very carefully against the wall.
Odalys stands, takes off one glove, and puts it back on.
Wren lets go of the pipe and her fingers stay curled in the shape of it.
Again.
units.name: ISHAAN
